description: Teach a brand-new person entity ('Ishaan') from a single realistic correction, with NO hand-authored seed entry anywhere in db/seed_data.py. Then test whether the system generalizes to a differently-misheard spelling ('Eshan', never seen in teaching) in an unseen sentence.

teach.original_text: Can ishan review the deployment notes before merging.
teach.corrected_text: Can Ishaan review the deployment notes before merging.
teach.notes: The only thing the system has ever been told about this person.

assert.asr_input: eshan should review the api docs and notes before merging
assert.expected_output: Ishaan should review the api docs and notes before merging.
assert.notes: Different misspelling than was taught ('Eshan' vs taught 'ishan'), in a sentence sharing two of the taught context words ('review', 'notes'). Phonetic similarity alone is moderate, not near-exact - this only crosses the intervention threshold because context corroborates it. Demonstrates the composite gate actually gating, not just phonetic lookup.

Same unseen misspelling as HOLD-01a, but zero overlap with the one context vocabulary the system has ever observed for this person. A single correction is deliberately not enough evidence to intervene in a completely unrelated context - this is the product choosing silence under weak evidence, not a bug. Compare to HOLD-02a, where a second ordinary correction changes this outcome for a *different* unrelated context.

description: A second, ordinary correction for the same person, in a different context ('standup'). Tests whether reinforcement through repeated ordinary use - not a bigger single upload - is what makes coverage broader, per the brief's 'how Kivi could learn through ordinary use'.

teach.notes: Second, independent correction. Also teaches the system that 'eshan' (not just 'ishan') is a misspelling of this person.

assert.asr_input: is eshan free for the standup
assert.expected_output: Is Ishaan free for the standup.
assert.notes: This is the exact sentence from HOLD-01b's context family ('free for ...'), which was suppressed before. It now intervenes because 'standup' overlaps a trigger learned in the second correction, AND 'eshan' is now itself a confirmed alias (not just a phonetic guess) - both learned from ordinary use, not from a bigger initial dictionary entry.

description: A holdout entity outside the 'person' category (a product/jargon term), taught via an explicit dictionary entry rather than a correction, to prove the mechanism isn't special-cased to names. Deliberately configured the way a developer might realistically configure a v1 entry: no negative_contexts yet (see HOLD-04).

teach.notes: Vector DB product name. v1 config - see HOLD-04/HOLD-05 for what happens next.

assert.asr_input: we store the embeddings in pine cone for fast retrieval
assert.expected_output: We store the embeddings in Pinecone for fast retrieval.
assert.notes: Multi-word ASR mishearing ('pine cone') in a legitimate product context.

description: No new teaching - reuses the memory state left by HOLD-03. 'Pine cone' is also a real, unrelated English noun phrase (a literal pine cone), and the v1 entry above has no negative_contexts to protect against that. This case is a DELIBERATE, LABELED demonstration of a real failure mode we discovered while building this suite, not a cherry-picked success - see README 'Known limitations & discovered failure modes' and eval/run_eval.py's report, which lists it separately from the pass/fail tally rather than folding it into the headline accuracy number.

assert.asr_input: i collected a fresh pine cone from the forest floor while hiking
assert.expected_output: I collected a fresh Pinecone from the forest floor while hiking.
assert.notes: This is the BUG, recorded as the system's actual (undesirable) behavior today given only the HOLD-03 teaching: it wrongly substitutes the literal pine cone. High phonetic similarity ('pine cone' is a registered alias) plus a merely-moderate base confidence is enough to clear the threshold even with zero relevant context, because no negative_contexts were ever taught for this entity. HOLD-05 shows the fix for exactly this.
assert.desired_output: I collected a fresh pine cone from the forest floor while hiking.

description: The product's answer to HOLD-04: the user reverts Kivi's wrong substitution, which teaches negative evidence (learn_negative_correction) instead of requiring a developer to hand-edit negative_contexts. Verifies the fix (a) actually suppresses the failing case, (b) generalizes to a DIFFERENT unseen forest sentence rather than memorizing the one correction, and (c) does not regress the legitimate product-context case - the fix must be scoped, not a blanket kill switch.

teach.memory_aware_text: I collected a fresh Pinecone from the forest floor while hiking.
teach.user_reverted_text: I collected a fresh pine cone from the forest floor while hiking.
teach.notes: The user undoing Kivi's HOLD-04 mistake - this is the entire teaching signal, not a manually written negative_contexts list.

assert.asr_input: i collected a fresh pine cone from the forest floor while hiking
assert.expected_output: I collected a fresh pine cone from the forest floor while hiking.
assert.notes: Same sentence as HOLD-04a - now correctly suppressed.

assert.asr_input: she picked up a pine cone near the forest trail and put it in her bag
assert.expected_output: She picked up a pine cone near the forest trail and put it in her bag.
assert.notes: A DIFFERENT, previously-unseen sentence that shares the learned negative context 'forest'. This checks that the veto generalizes from contextual evidence rather than memorizing the exact corrected sentence.

assert.asr_input: we store the embeddings in pine cone for fast retrieval
assert.expected_output: We store the embeddings in Pinecone for fast retrieval.
assert.notes: The original legitimate product-context case from HOLD-03 must still work. If this regressed, the negative-evidence mechanism would be an indiscriminate kill switch rather than a scoped correction - it is not.
